claim: Symbolic ILP learners (FOIL, then Popper, Metagol) can induce correct small rule sets from few examples with a cheap counted score; FOIL got 92.5% on chess endgame from 100 examples.
agent_test: Give the agent a counted coverage score (examples explained minus violated) to rank candidate rules, versus model self-ranking at equal tokens.

claim: Learning from failures (a failed hypothesis yields constraints that prune the search) beats plain enumeration by large factors (evens: 159 s vs 4 s; 10 buttons vs 3).
agent_test: On rule tasks, feed back which examples each failed rule mis-covers and forbid its generalisations; compare rounds-to-solution against resampling.

claim: ILP systems differ sharply in scaling: Metagol collapses near 10,000 examples, ILASP failed to ground, Popper stays fine at 20,000; so no single ILP backend is safe by default.
agent_test: Only relevant if the agent calls external ILP; otherwise note as a limit.

claim: Classical ILP (Popper, Aleph) degrades with noisy labels from about 10% noise; MDL-style MaxSynth tolerates up to about 30%; dILP gives a perfect answer on 5 of 6 tasks at 10% mislabelling. Update: MML vs C-MDL showed no significant difference at 10-50% noise (d09); MML only wins with few or one-sided examples.
agent_test: Inject 10% and 25% wrong labels into rule-induction items; test whether a count-based fit-versus-length rule choice beats accept-if-consistent.

claim: LLMs given examples do better when they first state a hypothesis, then write a program and test it, than when they answer directly (ARC subset: direct 17%, program 23%, summarised hypotheses 30%, human-selected 33%).
agent_test: On ARC-like items, compare direct vs hypothesis-then-program at equal tokens. Note all four lines are one paper (Wang et al.), so independence is 1.

claim: Hypothesis quality, not program writing, is the main bottleneck: a human-selected hypothesis led to a correct program in 33 of 49 tasks (67%); GPT-4 had a correct hypothesis for only 49 of 100. Replicated by Parab et al. 2025: GPT-4o generator correct in 46.4% of 64-sample trials; summariser drops 26% of correct ones.
agent_test: Measure how often the candidate set contains the right rule vs how often the agent selects it; spend tokens on selection if recall is high.

claim: Iterative hypothesis refinement with an external symbolic interpreter gives big gains where rules can be executed (GPT-4 ACRE task accuracy 28.0 to 59.0; MiniSCAN 0 to 46 and up to 95 with a symbolic parser).
agent_test: Run candidate rules in code on the examples before accepting them; compare to self-judged consistency.

claim: Refinement can hurt when the task is perceptual or the feedback is weak: MiniARC raw accuracy was 33.1 for direct and 5.9-18.7 with refinement. Also hypothesis refinement gave no gain on scientific tasks: Gemini-2.5-Flash 43.81 to 39.06, GPT-4.1 32.41 to 33.25 (d11).
agent_test: Add a check: if refinement lowers fit on held-out examples, revert to the first candidate.

claim: Models induce rules they cannot apply: MiniSCAN task accuracy fell from over 80% (symbolic interpreter) to near zero when the LM applied its own rules. Update: with altered arithmetic, GPT-5 learns from 512 examples as well as from the stated rule (87.2 vs 83.7), while GPT-4o-mini does not (47.8 vs 71.4); gap shrinks for reasoning models, but that test is implicit induction (d12).
agent_test: Separate rule-writing from rule-application; apply rules by code or by a fresh call and measure the gap.

claim: LLM rule induction is fragile to noisy examples: even one noisy example among 8 lowers performance, and telling the model about noise reduces but does not remove the drop. Replicated: at 10% noise DeepSeek-R1 loses 7.6 (CoT) or 5.6 (SRR) points on list functions, and answers flip item by item (d08).
agent_test: Insert 1 wrong example in 8; test whether a leave-one-out consistency check recovers accuracy.

claim: A rule library built from verified rules helps: Hypotheses-to-Theories raised GPT-4 on CLUTRR 50.6 to 64.3, and wrong rules caused 65% (CLUTRR) and 81% (base-16) of CoT errors; random rules drop it to 9.9.
agent_test: Keep a store of rules that were verified on examples; ablate with random rules and with unverified rules.

claim: Pairing an LLM with an exact logic solver on relational reasoning beats plain chain-of-thought and grows with chain length: CLUTRR 8-10 hops, Qwen 4B 19.1 to 61.9, GPT-5.4 59.9 to 75.1; GPT-4 gets 49% on IsUncle where a 60k-parameter ILP-style model gets 100%.
agent_test: Route relational rule steps to a small symbolic checker; compare accuracy by hop count at equal tokens.

claim: LLM + ILP loops reach perfect success with fewer refinement rounds than ILP alone (ALBI 1.4-1.7 iterations vs Popper 6.8, all 100% on 30 tasks) but cost more wall-clock time except for Popper's small tasks.
agent_test: Count tokens per solved task for LLM-proposes + counted-test vs pure sampling.

claim: LLM-proposed new predicates (predicate invention) need a verifier: unverified invention 58%, self-critique 73%, Prolog verification 80% on nine poker concepts; ILP alone 0/9.
agent_test: When the agent coins a helper concept, check it against examples by code before use.

claim: Against classical ILP under noise, large LLMs (GPT-3.5/4) have about 0.25 higher F1 on average and run about 1000 times faster, but small models are far weaker (GPT-4o is 21x Llama3-8B at noise 0.1) and no LLM beat Popper on CHAIN (multi-step chains).
agent_test: Check deep-chain items separately; expect model rules to fail on chains of independent predicates.

claim: Chain-of-thought does not reliably help pure induction: it lowered GPT-4o accuracy by up to 18-22% on MIRAGE, while ordinary test-time reasoning models improve logic-rule tasks but with steep cost (o3 gains 2x over GPT-4o for +1777% tokens). Reasoning models help: PBEBench Qwen3-32B 1.8 without CoT vs 41.9 with CoT (d02).
agent_test: Compare short direct induction, CoT, and generate-and-test at equal tokens on rule-induction items.

claim: Writing the rule is a separate ability from applying it: SolverLearner shows GPT-4 reaches near-perfect accuracy when it only induces a function and code runs it.
agent_test: Same as K09; use code execution for the apply step.

claim: Combining induction (program) and transduction (direct output) covers different ARC tasks; the ensemble reached 56.75% (2 tries) against average human 60.2%.
agent_test: Run both routes on each item and pick by counted fit on the training pairs.

claim: Explanations from machine-learned rules help people only when simple; for complex theories they can hurt (win_3 fell, p=0.005), and LLM-pipeline explanations gave no advantage over self-learning.
agent_test: Not for the agent; use only if we present rules to a human.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Rule-learning for agent safety: AutoSpec ILP rule evolution gives F1 0.98 and up to 94% fewer false positives on 291 traces.
agent_test: Out of scope until replicated; treat as a hint that rules from traces can be compiled into guards.

claim: At an equal budget of 6,000 LLM calls, half sampling plus half execution-guided repair beats all sampling on ARC-AGI for open models (Qwen 14B 5.63 to 14.25, 72B 12.88 to 25.25, Mistral-Large-2 18.50 to 25.62).
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of resampling vs test-and-repair with a current reasoning model.

claim: When single attempts often run out before ending, longer thinking beats more samples at matched compute (gpt-oss-120b on PBEBench); reasoning models score far above non-reasoning ones (Qwen3-32B 1.8 vs 41.9 with CoT).
agent_test: Per task, test one long thought against several short ones at equal tokens.

claim: Number of candidates needed scales as about 1/p, p being the share of proposals that are correct: k >= log(2/delta)/(-log(1-p)). Measured p for GPT-4o list functions is about 0.46 at 64 samples, and diverse candidates beat flat samples (11/19 vs 5/19 at 10 candidates, a code task).
agent_test: Estimate p on a few probe items, then set N; deduplicate candidates by behaviour on the examples.

claim: Length-penalised (MML/MDL) scoring helps when examples are few or one-sided (significant in 11 of 12 conditions at 20 and 50 examples) but is not better than C-MDL at 10-50% noise; it can learn from positive examples only. Not tested with an LLM proposer.
agent_test: Rank rule candidates by fit minus length; compare to pure fit at 10-30% planted label noise.

claim: Muggleton's ILP line: rules learned by Metagol let people succeed where examples alone failed (1 of 22 wrote the rule; mean score 1.76 to 5.24, p<0.001), invented predicates help only when they shorten the program, and with reused predicates one-shot string induction reached about 61% accuracy against 87% (humans, cyphered) and 76% (FlashFill).
agent_test: Name and keep invented concepts short; reuse earlier verified rules as building blocks.

claim: Rule-chain length is a wall: on ordered rule cascades GPT-5 and gpt-oss-120b stay under 5% on hard long cascades; o3-mini gets 5.69% compatibility on InductionBench's weighted leaderboard; extra examples stop helping as window size grows.
agent_test: Set a chain-length trigger: beyond a few ordered interacting steps, switch from LLM guessing to search or an exact solver.
